title: JARVIS distributed compute harness and MAIN continuity

context.problem: A single-MAIN compute harness must safely use a connected heterogeneous fleet: resource discovery, scoped scheduling, concurrent tasks, artifact transfer, receipts and MAIN continuity; mobile and cloud gateway remain interfaces/metadata roles.
constraints: Oracle: gateway, device status, pairing and job metadata only (user-selected)
AI sessions, prompts and personal memory remain on PCs
Arch preferred whenever healthy; Dell fallback must pass readiness
One user, initially two PCs; no absolute uptime guarantee
Fleet can enroll PCs and cloud servers; server enrollment does not grant AI/memory access
Manual preference changes are planned handovers; automatic failback follows configured preference
Exactly one active MAIN; all other compute machines, including Oracle, are NODEs
All ordinary mobile commands route via MAIN; only lease/membership recovery uses a separate control-plane path
Mobile MAIN transitions require separately enrolled fleet-admin permission and fresh target/epoch-bound authentication
Distributed compute is task-level, not pooled RAM/VRAM or live process migration
Control-ready MAIN and AI-ready MAIN are distinct readiness profiles on the same sole role
No overlapping old/new new-work grants; wait out old expiry or obtain target fence acknowledgements
Uncertain process capacity remains reserved until reconciled
Final workflow barrier required before planned continuation; abrupt-loss uncertainty is explicit
Stable logical task identity is separate from target-bound execution operation identity
Mobile-data loss does not change MAIN or replay interactive input

functional.text: Arch-preferred failover/failback for PC-local AI coordination
Keep AI sessions and personal memory on PCs
Extract role modules with injected versioned contracts and local/remote adapters
Enroll, scope, drain, upgrade and revoke PCs/cloud servers without code edits or cloned identities
Manually switch preferred coordinator after readiness/catch-up; keep execution and approval targets independent
Stable mobile interface routes ordinary requests through current MAIN to target; no ordinary work with no MAIN
Mobile can request temporary MAIN handover, saved preference change and expired-lease recovery via authenticated harness operations
Remove mobile location UI, geolocation and API disclosure
Discover permissioned CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM/OS/runtime resources with freshness and local admission
Deterministic scheduling of bounded parallel DAG tasks across eligible workers; explicit target never silently changes
Scoped encrypted artifact transfer, immutable manifests and hash verification; no cloud body persistence
Recover private workflow from PC journal/checkpoint and worker receipts; expose missing checkpoint instead of fabricating state

interfaces.name: Phone gateway
interfaces.contract: Tailnet HTTPS; paired cookie + verified Tailscale identity at gateway. Do not trust forwarded identity over arbitrary proxies. Same-origin typed endpoints only; never expose the trusted :7777 console.

interfaces.name: PC outbound link
interfaces.contract: Authenticated device-scoped connection; per-job operation ID, target, schema version, expiry, epoch and request digest; durable worker receipts; reconnect with capped jitter1–15s.

interfaces.name: Lease
interfaces.contract: Oracle transaction is sole authority; renew5s, valid15s, stale/unknown incarnation fails closed; gateway restart invalidates leases and waits for all old grants to expire.

interfaces.name: Personal state sync
interfaces.contract: PC-to-PC encrypted checkpoints and ordered changes; per-domain cursor and explicit staleness; never synchronize raw active SQLite or whole .jarvis; no gateway disk/log persistence. Personal records (memory, conversation, command/task history) are canonical in the Obsidian vault (single MAIN archive writer, same-DB outbox, no SQLite/vault atomicity claim); vault replication is transport only and cannot elect a writer.

deepDives.title: Failover without duplicate authority
deepDives.pressure: A network partition can make Arch appear dead while it is still running
deepDives.decision: Oracle single-writer transactional lease plus monotonic epoch/incarnation; executor validates on every new effect; MAIN-authorized screen sessions have their own scoped expiry grants
alternatives: Peer timeout election: two PCs cannot safely distinguish a partition
Full consensus cluster: not earned by a two-PC personal deployment
deepDives.failureMode: When Oracle is unreachable, reject new authority and let grants expire; availability loses to avoiding concurrent controllers. Already-issued external effects cannot be undone.
evidence: Failure detection yields suspicion, not truth

deepDives.title: Honest continuity of PC-local state
deepDives.pressure: Promoting Dell cannot recreate Arch-only memory or live provider sessions
deepDives.decision: Provider login readiness and PC-local replicated checkpoints gate AI promotion; controls work without AI; recreate sessions and show stale/unavailable memory explicitly
alternatives: Copy CLI auth/session directories: unsafe and not portable
deepDives.failureMode: Unsynced work can be unavailable when Arch dies. Preserve IDs and uncertain receipts; never silently rerun it.

deepDives.title: Stable phone origin with a small cloud gateway
deepDives.pressure: Phone origin and host-bound cookies currently live on Arch; video egress dominates RAM needs
deepDives.decision: One Oracle gateway process and SQLite, tailnet-only. Relay bounded media without recording; encrypted off-VM metadata backup daily. Benchmark input latency before optimizing MAIN-routed media paths.
alternatives: Move Tailscale machine identity/hostname between PCs: identity and credential conflict
deepDives.failureMode: Oracle outage blocks new remote authority; a cached PWA can display disconnected status only. Single-volume loss can lose <=24h metadata; require re-pair after untrusted rollback.

deepDives.title: Roles independent of device identity
deepDives.pressure: Adding a server or changing main currently touches fixed-main configuration, tunnels and in-process dependencies
deepDives.decision: Stable fleet identity, explicit preferred/active/target/approval roles, injected module contracts and phased legacy adapters; one codebase and few deployables
deepDives.failureMode: Partial migration can route to wrong target or create duplicate authority; protocol gates and epoch-checked executors block it
evidence: Two-PC envelope; Deep modules and Anti-overengineering gates

deepDives.title: Real reservations before scheduled work
deepDives.pressure: Stale fleet metrics and MAIN loss can overbook GPU/RAM or free capacity while a process still runs
deepDives.decision: Executor-side atomic admission, durable receipts and process-bound reservations; timeout quarantines allocation until reconciled
alternatives: Release resources whenever leader lease expires
deepDives.failureMode: Old task still consumes GPU while replacement is admitted

deepDives.title: Private workload state and transfer boundaries
deepDives.pressure: Oracle metadata cannot reconstruct source artifacts or private task DAG after loss of MAIN
deepDives.decision: PC-local checkpoint/journal plus verified worker receipts and immutable scoped artifact manifests; missing checkpoint restricts recovery
alternatives: Persist private DAG and outputs on Oracle
Rebuild instructions from redacted cloud job metadata
deepDives.failureMode: Fabricated recovery or duplicate side effects from incomplete scheduling state

pros: Stable mobile interface survives Arch sleep
One MAIN coordinates all ordinary work; membership service handles safe promotion
Cloud remains a scoped NODE; personal AI state stays on PCs
cons: Oracle is a single point of failure

Compute MVP adds admission, artifact and recovery contracts; enrollment and remote control alone do not satisfy it.

notes: Deploy optional-version readers before gateway writers; old nodes stay old-path-only until explicit enrollment. Protocol-version gate promotion. Keep legacy Arch endpoint for rollback; reconcile accepted job IDs before switching paths. Cloud pairing/history metadata after cutover is a new authority and must be exported before retiring it. No blind two-way metadata writes.

Single authority +15s expiring grants preserves one active coordinator through partitions
At200operations/day, one process/SQLite is sufficient; video bandwidth, not control-plane RAM, is the sizing risk

risks.text: Current main-only identity and in-process phone/hub coupling are explicit design constraints to migrate, not newly discovered debt.
Oracle availability, free-tier reclamation, CPU architecture and provider CLI support remain unverified.
Trusted executors can fence stale runtimes; this does not stop malicious unsandboxed code already running as the owner.
Memory checkpoint RPO target<=30s applies only while both PCs connected; unsynced state remains unavailable after an isolated crash.
Modular extraction must preserve behavior before moving placement; no big-bang rewrite.
A second cloud server is not automatically a second authority; initial gateway remains a single failure domain.
Provider credentials/session portability and personal-state write conflicts must be solved before automatic AI promotion.
Grant expiry/clock margin and target fencing acknowledgements need protocol proof before no-dual-MAIN claims.
Actual reservations, artifacts and two-host parallel work are mandatory compute evidence; mocks are insufficient.
Owner accepts identity revocation rollback after stale Oracle backup restore; old leadership grants still must not revive.

nextSteps: P0 Inventory and threat/failure baseline — Existing topology/Hub/CLI/local effects, supervisors, data and provider stores; Oracle resources/network; current tests
P1 In-place module contracts — Facades around topology, registry, Remote, provider lanes, state, phone/Console
P2 Protocol/identity/durable modes — Stable installation identity, mode guard outside per-command --state, original tickets, attempts, receipts and negotiation
P3 Authority prototype and worker concurrency — Oracle CAS authority in isolated test fleet; control/job lanes, local resource/workspace admission and process supervision
P4 Exclusive production cutover and manual controls — Guard-aware compatibility release, disable old managed paths, target fence acknowledgements, one v2 MAIN, gateway pilot
P5 Concurrent compute MVP — Resource snapshots, deterministic scheduler/DAG, scoped artifacts, isolated attempts, global logical-result journal
P6 Prepared state and safe agents — PC-only state/workflow journals/replicas, final barrier, separate provider readiness, broker-mediated fleet-effect tools
P7 Mobile MAIN management — Role status/preview/confirm/status, manage_main+passkey, immutable transition IDs
P8 Shadow and opt-in automatic handover — Preference/failover state machine, sleep/resume invalidation, permit drain, journal barrier and reconciliation
P9 Production soak and restore — PWA origin migration, signed updates, off-VM metadata/PC backups, privacy and resource limits
P10 Optional extensions — Extra cloud compute, specialized GPU runtimes, data-parallel adapters or gateway HA

operationIdentity.issuer: authority-generated operation ID and signed original ticket
operationIdentity.afterGC: expired ticket rejected before receipt lookup; missing ticket cannot recreate historical ID
operationIdentity.acceptedLongRunningWork: admission expiry does not cancel accepted work; reconcile process and result journal
operationIdentity.identityHierarchy: operation_id here is execution-specific; logical request/workload/task IDs persist across policy-authorized new target attempts

workspacePolicy.publication: attempt-local immutable artifacts and target-journal logical-result CAS
workspacePolicy.merge: separate owner-reviewed authorized apply against unchanged base revision

mainHandoffPlan.initialAdmission: MAIN selects/signs; target prepares receipt then online authority consumes new-operation identity; reconcile partial commits
mainHandoffPlan.offlineStreams: bounded sequence permits; no per-frame DB writes
mainHandoffPlan.sleepResume: invalidate cached authorization; tested suspend-aware elapsed time; online revalidation
mainHandoffPlan.legacyLimit: Guard-aware managed paths fenced persistently; unmodified owner-privileged old code requires actual shutdown/disable, not a marker-only claim

identityHierarchy.sameExecutionRetry: same ticket, original age and target
identityHierarchy.crossWorkerRetry: new attempt and execution operation/ticket, same logical task; reconcile old attempt first

workflowHandover.planned: freeze old writer; durable HANDOVER_BARRIER sequence/hash; candidate fsync acknowledgement; resume only after authority fencing
workflowHandover.unplanned: affected active workflows uncertain until PC journal/receipts prove commit state; missing proof blocks continuation
workflowHandover.lateResults: retained at target; successor reconciles; old MAIN cannot commit after barrier
workflowHandover.availability: new control-ready MAIN is not proof old workflows recovered

providerExecutionClasses.unmediatedLegacy: stop managed process tree on loss; retain uncertainty; not approved for strict post-demotion effect fencing
